A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TPA research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support matching retained content across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original TPA evaluations on RAGTruth and Dolly (AC), source-removal ablations and SHAP analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these empirical results and adds Qwen3-8B evaluation, aggregation ablations and validation of an automated hallucination judge.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same seven-source attribution, head-logit apportionment, POS aggregation and classifier pipeline. The Qwen3 implementation applies this procedure to another backbone; TPA-Mean and TPA-Stat are experimental ablations, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: RAGTruth and Dolly (AC) remain the evaluated datasets and tasks. Qwen3 uses existing RAGTruth queries and retrieved contexts, changing the model configuration and labeling procedure rather than task or domain coverage. Clinical, legal, non-English and code scenarios are motivation or future work.

E2.justification: v4 adds TPA-Mean and TPA-Stat as simple aggregation comparators in Table 5. Existing external-baseline membership is unchanged, including TSV and Novo for Mistral; the new Qwen3 comparison reuses that pair.

E3.justification: The added Qwen3 evaluation introduces greedy decoding with thinking disabled, Claude Opus 4.6 labels and class weighting. Judge validation uses 450 human-annotated Llama2-7B responses, and aggregation controls use 7 or 14 features instead of 126. Existing split, cross-validation and tuning protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v3's source-removal and SHAP analyses, v4 directly tests the central POS-aggregation choice against global mean and mean-plus-standard-deviation pooling across seven settings (Section 5, Table 5). This substantially expands component validation. It also adds a human-annotation agreement check for the new automated judge.

E5.justification: Five outer seeds, five-member ensembles, standard-deviation reporting and one-sample t-tests are retained. New tables reuse five-run averages and existing significance conventions. Cohen's kappa is a new judge-evaluation metric; TPA-Stat's standard deviations are input features, not additional uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are unchanged. v4 Table 3 adds Qwen3 F1 scores of 0.6006 for TPA, 0.5493 for TSV and 0.5468 for Novo, alongside AUC and recall. Table 5 adds pooling-variant results: for Dolly Llama2-13B, POS/Mean/Stat F1 is 0.8075/0.5828/0.6009. Judge validation adds accuracy 0.82, F1 0.83 and kappa 0.64. These are substantial additional findings, not improvements to earlier same-setting scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–20, Theorem 1, Proposition 1, both appendix proofs and the complexity derivation are unchanged. The new seven-source rationale explains the existing partition without changing its mathematical definition or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the central claims of complete seven-source attribution, syntax-aware detection and interpretable strong performance. Naming five evaluated LLMs in v4 makes the supporting evaluation more specific without introducing a new central contribution.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly excludes retrieval errors, outdated knowledge and ambiguous evidence from its hallucination scope. It adds explanations for separating Past from Self and preserving source-POS interactions, and discusses future noisy-retrieval and multilingual applications. The original three limitations and SHAP interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 supplies an explicit code-access link and Qwen-specific template, decoding, Transformers-fork and class-weighting details. It changes the software description from PyTorch 3.10 to Python 3.10 and PyTorch 2.x. Hardware, sequential extraction, approximately 20-second runtime and GPU-hour estimates were already documented in v3.

R1.justification: v4 substantially broadens related-work coverage through a new distribution-shift and predictive-distribution modeling subsection, covering distillation, concept drift and structural representations. It also adds prototype-learning, legal/agent and Qwen3 references while retaining the original hallucination-detection literature and positioning.

P1.justification: v4 expands the abstract and introductory motivation, adds explanatory paragraphs, edits baseline descriptions and extends future-work prose. Post-reference sections 9–14 become Appendices A–F. The main narrative order and most existing text remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds the compact Qwen3 comparison table and aggregation-ablation table. The hyperparameter and full-results tables are renumbered, and existing displays move with text reflow. Figures 1–5 and both algorithm displays retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: Table 5 directly supports the previously unablated POS-aggregation choice, while the Qwen3 experiment and explicit code/setup information strengthen validation and reproducibility. The gain is limited because Qwen3 labels are automated and their human-agreement check uses Llama2 responses. The original experimental evidence and theory are preserved.
